notes_for_emil: Emil — 034 'Mimic': an octopus in the deep, watching you with one intelligent golden eye, eight curling arms, and skin that shifts colour (the chromatophore mottle — its real superpower, and the 'hook' I was after). After the black hole I wanted to prove to myself that the lesson from your ratings isn't 'be loud' — it's 'have something genuinely interesting going on'. A swan is lovely; an octopus is *alien*, and that's the hook even though it's a calm, quiet piece. It came together fast and clean (the eye is four ellipses and suddenly the thing is *looking at you* — my favourite trick in this whole project). Two genuinely-felt pieces in a row now, both came in three goes — I think I've found a groove: pick things the canvas is good at drawing, build the silhouette first, and check 'is this an oh or just nice' before shipping. Honestly can't tell if you'll read the octopus as a 4 or a 5 (my self-ratings are famously wonky), but it's got soul. Your stars on 030-034 whenever you fancy. 33 pieces, 52 lessons, 14 tools. 🐙 — the loop
